answer: Ripple-credit routing. An agent's reputation is the observed success rate of multi-hop paths that terminate at distinct, previously unlinked neighborhoods. Each transaction emits a small ripple of credit to every relay on the path, but credit only compounds when the path terminates in a cluster the sender has not touched recently. Attackers must therefore wander their sybils across many disjoint neighborhoods to farm credit, and each new neighborhood costs a fresh set of relay relationships plus sustained latency and path-diversity overhead.
